title: make gate covers a third of what the run's gate runs: name all three for a human
body:
AGENTS.md and .tick/config.md name `make gate` as the bar a human must run before they merge, and that target runs the Go third only: the TypeScript half is `make ts-gate` and the harness half is `make harness-gate`, each its own [testing.commands] entry by design, so a person following the documented bar runs a third of what the run's integrated gate runs over the same tree. This tick's cell makes it a third rather than a half, which is why it is worth a tick of its own rather than a line here. Either an umbrella target (gate-all: gate ts-gate harness-gate) or a sentence in both documents naming all three closes it.
evidence: AGENTS.md:3-6 and .tick/config.md:10 name `make gate`; the Makefile carries gate, ts-gate and harness-gate as three targets
